headline: US Energy Secretary Chris Wright told data center supporters to push back against critics, calling concerns about the projects overblown.
score_reason: Lowered from 5 to 3: the remarks were made on 30 Jun 2026, so this is old news.
importance_line: The US energy secretary is openly backing data-center builders against local opposition, which matters to communities near planned sites, but his claims about water and prices are his own and a Gallup poll found most respondents opposed local projects.
summary: Business Insider reports that Energy Secretary Chris Wright told an Amazon Web Services conference that worries about data centers are real but "overblown", urged their supporters to push back, and compared the argument with the fracking fight 15 years ago. He said water use is "tiny" next to the benefits, while a Gallup survey in May found seven in ten US adults opposed building AI data centers in their area; the remarks were made on 30 Jun 2026.
notes: Old news re-dated by EnergyNow; read Business Insider's version.
